[PATH:empirical] Systematic benchmark study comparing multi-paradigm architectures (e.g., neural-symbolic, hybrid Bayesian-deep learning) against state-of-the-art single-paradigm models (e.g., pure deep learning, pure kernel methods) on standardized out-of-distribution low-data benchmarks like Mini-ImageNet, CIFAR-FS, or Meta-Dataset — Direct empirical comparison under controlled conditions can measure whether hybrid approaches consistently yield lower generalization error than the best single-paradigm methods, addressing the core claim.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of bias-variance tradeoffs and inductive bias in multi-paradigm architectures, using frameworks from statistical learning theory (e.g., PAC-Bayes, Rademacher complexity) to bound generalization error as a function of model complexity and data sparsity — A formal proof or counterexample showing that combining diverse inductive biases necessarily reduces or cannot reduce generalization error compared to the optimal single paradigm would confirm or refute the hypothesis under idealized assumptions.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of published results from few-shot learning, transfer learning, and meta-learning literature (e.g., from NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR proceedings 2020-2025) that compare hybrid and single-paradigm approaches on low-data tasks — Synthesizing existing evidence across many studies can reveal consistent patterns or lack thereof, and identify confounding factors (e.g., dataset choice, architectural details) that may explain conflicting findings.
